title: Fiberwise independence of the two special bits
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for disjointness inputs of length $n$, an achievable value $z$ of the associated $Z$-variable, and a pair of bits $b=(b_1,b_2)$. Let $F$ be the fiber consisting of those hard-distribution samples $\omega$ whose $Z$-variable equals $z$, and for such a sample write $x_T(\omega)$ for Alice's bit at the special coordinate and $y_T(\omega)$ for Bob's bit at the special coordinate. Then
\[
\abs{\{\omega\in F : x_T(\omega)=b_1\}}\cdot\abs{\{\omega\in F : y_T(\omega)=b_2\}}
=\abs{\{\omega\in F : (x_T(\omega),y_T(\omega))=b\}}\cdot\abs{F}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: p a deterministic disjointness protocol of length n
z an achievable value of the Z-variable for p
b = (b_1, b_2) a pair of bits
replaced: The switching map $(ωX, ωY) ↦ (mix ωX ωY, mix ωY ωX)$ gives the cardinal identity underlying conditional independence of \texttt{specialX} and \texttt{specialY} on a $Z=z$ fiber.
